data.narrative:
Wyvern is a Series A space and aerospace company founded by Chris Robson, Callie Lissinna, Kurtis Broda, and Kristen Cote, having raised $16M to date. The valuation landscape includes five public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight identified private peers, though the narrow peer set at the Series A stage limits direct median comps.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proves applicable. Using total capital raised ($16M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage advancement yields $32M. Peer-median analysis cannot proceed; while 11 same-sector peers exist, none of the stage-aligned or tier-aligned subsets contain the minimum three datapoints required for statistical validity. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable due to the absence of disclosed revenue for the target—standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $27M to $37M, centered at $32M. The median point reflects conservative application of stage-progression mechanics against the $16M invested base. Key uncertainties include Wyvern's actual revenue run-rate, capital efficiency versus public Space & Aerospace peers trading at 23.9x median P/S, and whether the 2.0x multiplier appropriately reflects current early-stage space sector dynamics. Additional disclosure of customer traction or technical milestones would improve precision.
